recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.

A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "From The Silver Spoon To The Bottom", "body": "Butler tells Chance Garton that by his early forties he had multiple properties, multiple businesses, an inheritance from his grandfather and, in his own words, every possible advantage, while internally conflicted and drinking through morning, afternoon and night. He describes losing two good jobs inside a year and a half, two bad breakups and a confrontation over 900 dollars that made him snap. The Monday after, he left Cape Cod and drove toward California to hug a redwood tree, 26 hours to Kansas City, then lived on the road for roughly eighteen months while contemplating removing himself from the planet. He is now a little over three years sober."}, {"title": "The Question That Comes Before Everything", "body": "Both men circle the identity question Butler puts at the front of Butler's DMT Field Guide, whose chapters ask who the hell am I and who the hell are you, and whose seventh chapter opens with the word chance. Garton, who identifies with the number seven, riffs that chance is the absence of concept, a state not yet defined. Butler says he is opening his next book, on psychedelic integration, with the same question, and admits he once paid a therapist 240 dollars an hour while trying to outsmart him and present a false picture of himself. Ask it before anything else, he argues, and not rhetorically."}, {"title": "The Molecule The Body Already Makes", "body": "Butler says the endogenous nature of dimethyltryptamine is what first gripped him, and points to Rick Strassman's study in the 1990s and its account of the compound being pulsed at points in the life cycle, including shortly after conception. He connects it to near death experiences, trauma and childbirth, while Garton relays accounts from mothers who gave birth unsedated and described crossing a veil. Butler says he is not the physiologist, naming Andrew Gallimore and Imperial College as the people asking whether consciousness is produced in the brain or received through it. He also flags temporal lobe epilepsy, migraine and autism reports that echo the same territory."}, {"title": "Rocket Fuel, Not A Magic Pill", "body": "Asked for disclaimers before the miracle stories start, Butler says psychedelics certainly are not for everybody, that he does not condone use, is not trying to sensationalize anything, and that everybody has to do their own homework, including on medication interactions. He calls it rocket fuel that can carry a rocket ship out of space or blow it up on the way, and insists it is a tool rather than a crutch. Garton neither recommends nor discourages it, compares an intense session to opening a multiverse portal that swaps in a parallel version of you, and warns that a lit up energy body attracts curious moths."}, {"title": "Entities, Future Selves And Synchronicity", "body": "Butler describes a progression across a year and a half and more than a hundred sessions: first exploring the space, then feeling like the one being examined, an animal in a zoo or a firefly with a flashing head, and finally meeting what he takes to be himself from another time running a calibration check, which he credits with removing his fear of death. The two trade synchronicity stories, Butler on a radio segment mentioning a llama seconds after he passed a llama farm, Garton on handing a stranger a lost backpack at a festival before the man could ask. Garton calls separateness the real illusion."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Adam Butler, author of Butler's DMT Field Guide, joins InnerVerse to talk about how the most powerful (and natural) of psychedelics was part of his path of transformation from living with a stressed out deathwish to experiencing the wonder of life with awestruck gratitude. We discuss what DMT does endogenously in the body, what the blast off, hyperspace beings, and cosmic consciousness are like, the eternal question of "who am I?" and much more.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Riding the Frequency Up and Down", "body": "Adam describes the steady electric hum that arrives with DMT and says his aim now is for his body to resonate with that frequency rather than merely hear it, sometimes vibrating so strongly he holds onto his partner. He links this to the Monroe Institute's binaural beat research and hopes to attend a program there. Chance shares a journey where a Buddha at the center of a spinning kaleidoscope told him to go with the flow, then a descending tone carried him back into his body, and the person beside him said she had never heard a sound like that come from a human voice."}, {"title": "Solfeggio Numbers and a Clear Mind", "body": "Chance cautions that online claims about 528 hertz repairing DNA are unprovable, yet he finds real clues in the number relationships of the Solfeggio set. Because binaural effects come from the difference between two tones, he likes pairing 528 with 417, a gap of 111, and he ties that number to Hebrew gematria, where aleph equals 111 and points to the hidden oneness of the creator. He argues tuning forks are psychedelic in the literal sense of making the mind clear, describing sessions full of synchronicity and a client whose ankle grew hot as balanced energy returned."}, {"title": "Where Language and Time Come From", "body": "Adam wonders how entities convey information without English, through glyphs, sights and sounds. Chance points to his friend Hakan Hassim's Universal Transmissions project, a codex of alien script, and asks whether speech and writing were taught to us from what we call DMT space, which would explain why the source is called the Logos. He suggests our filters are a cultural overlay of identity that a primordial human may not have had. The pair then turn to cosmic cycles, a day of Brahman spanning ages, and Adam, drawing on his years carving wood and stone, questions the official dating of sites like Gobekli Tepe."}, {"title": "Befriending the Boogeyman", "body": "Chance calls himself less a killer of sacred cows than a slayer of boogeymen, arguing that anyone attached to a boogeyman will meet it in the psychedelic experience and can choose to see it as an extension of themselves. Adam reframes this: do not slay the boogeyman, befriend it, since you may need to call on it one day, and he compares the psyche to the characters of Inside Out. Chance adds that every perpetrator justifies harm through a victim identity, so realizing you are happening to the boogeyman, not the reverse, frees trapped energy. Adam also reads Shiva's destructive dance as joyful renewal."}, {"title": "Energy Exchange, Not Energy Suck", "body": "Chance explains the Ophite Gnostic view that the Genesis serpent was the good guy, identifying it with Eros, the spark between opposite poles that lets humanity continue. When critics warn Adam that entering these spaces exposes him to entities feeding on his energy, he answers that podcasts, the gym and psychedelics all cost energy, so it is really an exchange he stays aware of and controls. Chance adds that our true self lives in the realm of ideas, so there is no permanent loss. Adam, a trained entomologist, compares strange entities to beautiful but alien insects he would rather greet than fear."}]

fields.Plus Quotes JSON: [{"text": "I think that if we knew the numbers behind the words that we were speaking, we would be getting spoken to by whatever the things we're calling DMT aliens are.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The jestery characters are jestery. The dark characters look dark. I haven't come across a sense of falsity.", "author": "Adam Butler", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/8785f1f8-c35c-4dcd-91d3-8c38b678d555/ADAM-BUTLER.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "All the filters that we have are based on identity, and that identity is mostly a cultural overlay that we pick up.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I don't think everybody needs to go through a psychedelic rebirth like I did, but if we can just understand that we're connected and love, it sounds so simple, but that's what we need.", "author": "Adam Butler", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/8785f1f8-c35c-4dcd-91d3-8c38b678d555/ADAM-BUTLER.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "When I got outside of time or outside of this limited storyline Earth, everybody else was out of it, too.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "It's not necessarily slaying the boogeyman. Befriend the boogeyman.", "author": "Adam Butler", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/8785f1f8-c35c-4dcd-91d3-8c38b678d555/ADAM-BUTLER.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Every perpetrator is in some way justifying their behavior through a victim identity. That's just a reality.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Honestly, doing a two-hour podcast is an energy suck. Going to the gym is an energy suck. Doing psychedelics is an energy suck. And I say energy suck. It's an energy exchange.", "author": "Adam Butler", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/8785f1f8-c35c-4dcd-91d3-8c38b678d555/ADAM-BUTLER.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "If some entity grabs my hand from underneath the bed, I'd be like, \"Cool, why are you here, and what do you want to talk to me about?\"", "author": "Adam Butler", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/8785f1f8-c35c-4dcd-91d3-8c38b678d555/ADAM-BUTLER.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Ultimately, a deep and true connection with spirit is synonymous with embracing the free will or the truth that everything is a choice.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}]
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "All of my problems were internal problems and the solutions were internal, and ultimately I was looking for something in the external world.", "author": "Adam Butler", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/8785f1f8-c35c-4dcd-91d3-8c38b678d555/ADAM-BUTLER.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Chance is the absence of concept, it's a potentiated state without a definition, that when you're in the realm of chance you're in the realm of what's not yet been decided or defined.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Why is your body producing this? And I think that was one of the main reasons why Rick Strassman did his study in the 90s.", "author": "Adam Butler", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/8785f1f8-c35c-4dcd-91d3-8c38b678d555/ADAM-BUTLER.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The way I metaphorize it is like you're opening a multi-dimensional or multiverse portal, you're sending away the old you and bringing in a parallel universe version of you to come in and be you.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "It is not a magic pill, and if you're turning to psychedelics like some people do prescription pills, alcohol, it's just going to be the same thing. It's not a crutch you can lean on.", "author": "Adam Butler", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/8785f1f8-c35c-4dcd-91d3-8c38b678d555/ADAM-BUTLER.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "In the near death experience you have this psychopomp that shows up, whether it's the person's belief in Buddha or Jesus or even Odin or something.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I'm very comfortable with who I am. There'll never be any person or place or thing that would ever make me lie or put my integrity of character on the line.", "author": "Adam Butler", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/8785f1f8-c35c-4dcd-91d3-8c38b678d555/ADAM-BUTLER.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I truly believe we're only as sick as our secrets, and if our first instinct is honesty then I don't think we're going to get led down any really destructive pathways.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}]
